competition.summary: AMD keeps taking x86 share in every segment (Mercury Research, Q2 2026: +7.3 pts YoY in servers and +8.4 pts in mobile). Intel still ships about two-thirds of x86 units. In foundry, TSMC dominates leading-edge manufacturing at 56% operating margins; Intel's pitch is a US-based alternative (18A/18A-P now, 14A in 2027–28) with Tesla as the first 14A customer and a reported Apple deal. Arm-based chips (Apple silicon, Qualcomm) are a structural threat in client, and Apple is dropping Intel Mac support.

summary: Intel's turnaround is real: Q2 revenue grew 25%, data-center sales jumped 59%, gross margin recovered about 12 points to ~42%, and it has landed Tesla (14A) plus a reported Apple foundry deal. At $123 (up ~250% in a year) the stock trades at ~73x forward earnings and ~11.7x sales on a 7.8% operating margin, above the average analyst target ($116) and well above what peer multiples or a base-case earnings-power model support (~$80–120). Strategic holders (Nvidia, SoftBank, the US government) and momentum can keep it elevated, but the price already assumes the foundry succeeds, while ~$20B of new shares and heavy capex dilute the payoff. Fairly valued at best near $120; we'd be underweight and wait for pullbacks or 14A customer proof.

valuation.method: Triangulated three ways. (a) Peer multiples: peer forward P/E median ~21x (57x for AMD); giving Intel a 25–45x turnaround premium on ~$2.08 2027 EPS (implied by 59x per Motley Fool) = $52–94. Intel's EV/sales (11.7x) is close to TSMC's (13.9x) with one-seventh of the margin. (b) Earnings power (2029): base $80B revenue × 25% op margin, 15% tax, 5.3B shares → ~$3.2 EPS × 30x = $96, discounted 2 years at 10% ≈ $80; bull $100B × 30% → ~$4.8 × 35x = $168 → ~$139; bear $65B × 15% → ~$1.6 × 20x ≈ $31. (c) Analysts: $75–$200, mean $116, median $112.
valuation.note: Blended fair value $80–120 (mid $100) gives weight to the strategic premium (US-government, Nvidia and Apple ties) that pure multiples ignore. Price $122.95 is above the top of the range. Peer data from StockAnalysis, Sep 25–26, 2026; TSMC growth is in TWD.
